Lower priority: naming nits, comment polish. Preserve any serious defect regardless of priority.

# Rules for every delegated run (2026-11-20)

You are one implementer in the Farhan build loop. Read your own brief first, then this file.

- Repo: Android app, Kotlin, Compose. Work only in the worktree your brief names. Never touch `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan` (the main tree) and never run `git stash`, `git push`, `gh`, or open a PR or issue.

- Flag any problem you spend more than 30 minutes on (the same failing test or symptom across 3 or more runs) in your report, keep working on the rest, and the orchestrator will cut it or ask.
- Roughly five minutes into your work the orchestrator will read a few of your files and ask 2-3 concrete questions through your thread. Answer from the work. Raise a real blocker immediately.
- Write your report file early (path in your brief) and keep it current; a cut-off run must leave one. State what you did, what you could not verify, every default you took, and every place you changed an existing test.
- Tests: follow the `test-quality` skill. Each test carries `// why:` (the bug or rule it guards) and `// catches:` (a plausible wrong implementation it fails). Never loosen an existing assertion to make code pass.
- Interfaces: follow `technical-excellence`: exhaustive `when` with no default branch, parse at the boundary, invalid states unrepresentable, claims cited as `// CLAIM(id): ... [source]`. No comments that narrate your session.
- Copy: any user-visible string is copy. Load the `writing-copy` skill for it. No eyebrow lines.

## Building and testing (this host has 7 GB RAM: do not run Gradle here)

All Gradle and emulator work runs on the Boat sandbox `bx_bngcafgz` (large, already resumed, Nix socket already repaired). One Gradle build at a time across all agents: wrap every build in the lock.

```
flock /tmp/farhan-boat.lock python3 -I /home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/bin/boat-run \
  --sandbox bx_bngcafgz --shell 'nix develop -c' --name <your-run-name> --large <your worktree> -- \
  ./gradlew <tasks> --no-daemon -q
```

`<your-run-name>` must be unique to you (it names a warm run directory on the sandbox: `~/runs/<name>`). The command prints the pass/fail and a log path. Test reports are under `~/runs/<name>/<module>/build/test-results/`; read them with `boat exec bx_bngcafgz --timeout 60 -- bash -lc '...'` (prints one JSON line; `boat scp` copies files). ## Committing

# Per-category Clear: brief

Read first: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/agent-rules-2026-11-20.md`.

You are the implementer (Sol): red tests first, then green, in this one run. Stop at green with tests passing; the orchestrator reviews next.

## The bug (owner, 2026-11-20)

"The clear button, in a particular category, only clears what is in that category, not everything overall."

In the notification inbox (`notification_filter_presentation/.../NotificationFilterScreen.kt`) the filter chips are Critical, High, Medium, Low, All, and Cleared. The bottom
button "Clear all" (line ~429) sends `OnDeleteAllNotifications` -> `DeleteAllNotifications` use case -> `core.coordinator.clearAll { repository.deleteAllNotificationsFromDB(); service.clearNotificationActions() }`
-> DAO `DELETE FROM notificationitementity`. So it removes every row, invalidates every pending delivery (`invalidateAll()`), and drops every retained action, whichever chip is selected.

## Required behaviour

1. With a priority chip selected the button clears exactly the rows that chip lists, on every page (the list shows 100 per page; the clear must not stop at the page). "All" keeps clearing everything. In the Cleared view the button acts only on the rows that view lists (no live inbox rows are touched).
2. The membership rule is the list's rule, which includes standing escalation: `NotificationInboxFilter.effectivePriority` (unread, not CRITICAL, older than the standing threshold hours counts one level lower) and the SQL `NotificationQueries.INBOX` with `standingCutoff`. Use ONE shared definition so list and clear cannot drift (a shared SQL fragment/constant, or a DAO query that takes the same arguments). Capture the standing cutoff once when the button is pressed so a row cannot change category between the list and the delete.
3. Clear only the affected ids in the delivery coordinator: do not call `invalidateAll()` for a scoped clear (that would cancel pending deliveries of rows the owner did not clear). Add a scoped coordinator operation and test that a pending High delivery survives a "clear Low". Retained notification actions are removed only for the cleared ids (`ServiceUtil.clearNotificationActions()` is all-or-nothing today; add a per-ids variant).
4. Button label names the scope: "Clear all" for All, "Clear high" etc. for a priority, and for the Cleared view something accurate (decide, log it as a default). Strings are copy (`writing-copy`).
5. No confirmation dialog (unchanged). Counts shown elsewhere (dashboard) update through the existing flows.

## Not in scope (report, do not change)

The dashboard's `FloodStatusWidget` "Clear All" (`OnDeleteAll`) and `StandingAlarmsWidget` "Clear All" (`OnClearAllStanding`); say in the report whether they have the same flaw.

## Tests

Test the design: (a) a parity test that the delete predicate and the list predicate select the same rows for a seeded set that includes standing-escalated rows (find how the existing data tests run Room/DAO; if none exist on the JVM, use the pure filter as the oracle and assert both queries are built from the shared fragment); (b) coordinator: scoped clear leaves other pending deliveries valid; (c) use case: scope -> repository call -> action removal for those ids only; (d) the screen's event carries the selected scope. Targeted runs only (`:notification_filter:*:test`).
# Per-category Clear

Base `717faf6`, branch `fix/clear-per-category`. The notification inbox clears the selected priority across every page. **Clear all** still clears the entire inbox. **Delete cleared history** clears the entries listed in Cleared, which continues to use the prior priority filter when one is set.

The click captures the cutoff used by the displayed query. Listing, selecting IDs, and deleting share one SQL predicate. Room selects IDs and deletes matching rows in the same transaction under the coordinator gate, using the predicate for both statements to avoid SQLite's ID parameter limit. The coordinator invalidates callbacks and removes retained actions by affected ID. It preserves callback capture order for eviction and allows newer callbacks to run after the transaction. Canceling those IDs' Android proxies is cleanup, so the callback mapper ignores Farhan's own cancellation while keeping user swipes actionable. A tab change hides the previous list until the new query loads.

## Regression tests

- The first Boat run used the new entry-point signatures with the old global behavior. Five assertions failed as expected for SQL membership, pending High delivery, scoped repository and action calls, click scope, and label mapping. Log `/tmp/boat-run/clear-category-20261120T115435Z-c18a9d.log`.
- The focused proxy callback run failed as expected when Farhan's own proxy cancellation was classified as a source app removal. Log `/tmp/boat-run/clear-category-20261120T115806Z-1c32f0.log`.
- The final Boat run passed all 179 targeted JVM tests with zero skips. Domain 155, data 21, presentation 3. Tasks were `:notification_filter:notification_filter_{domain,data,presentation}:testDebugUnitTest`. Log `/tmp/boat-run/clear-category-20261120T120013Z-5e8772.log`. `git diff --check` passed.
- Changes to existing test files were limited to extending the SQLite JDBC fixture's parameter binding for deletes, adding regression cases to the SQL, coordinator, and removal mapper suites, and implementing the new repository method in the dashboard-summary fake as an unsupported write. Existing assertions and red expectations are intact.

## Scope and limits

The flood widget dispatches a global delete, which also removes rows outside the flood window. The standing widget pages through its standing predicate and deletes the matching rows individually. The dashboard handlers were outside this change.

The JVM run exercises the actual SQL via SQLite JDBC and the screen's click dispatch and label mapping via presentation state. The app-generated Room DAO, rendering on a device, and real Android notification callbacks remain unverified. No issue reached the 30-minute flag threshold.

content.content:
1	# Per-category Clear: brief
2	
3	Read first: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/agent-rules-2026-11-20.md`.
4	Worktree: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/clear-category`, branch `fix/clear-per-category`, base `717faf6`.
5	Report file: `research/clear-category-report.md`. Boat run name: `clear-category`.
6	You are the implementer (Sol): red tests first, then green, in this one run. Stop at green with tests passing; the orchestrator reviews next.
7	
8	## The bug (owner, 2026-11-20)
9	
10	"The clear button, in a particular category, only clears what is in that category, not everything overall."
11	
12	In the notification inbox (`notification_filter_presentation/.../NotificationFilterScreen.kt`) the filter chips are Critical, High, Medium, Low, All, and Cleared. The bottom
13	button "Clear all" (line ~429) sends `OnDeleteAllNotifications` -> `DeleteAllNotifications` use case -> `core.coordinator.clearAll { repository.deleteAllNotificationsFromDB(); service.clearNotificationActions() }`
14	-> DAO `DELETE FROM notificationitementity`. So it removes every row, invalidates every pending delivery (`invalidateAll()`), and drops every retained action, whichever chip is selected.
15	
16	## Required behaviour
17	
18	1. With a priority chip selected the button clears exactly the rows that chip lists, on every page (the list shows 100 per page; the clear must not stop at the page). "All" keeps clearing everything. In the Cleared view the button acts only on the rows that view lists (no live inbox rows are touched).
19	2. The membership rule is the list's rule, which includes standing escalation: `NotificationInboxFilter.effectivePriority` (unread, not CRITICAL, older than the standing threshold hours counts one level lower) and the SQL `NotificationQueries.INBOX` with `standingCutoff`. Use ONE shared definition so list and clear cannot drift (a shared SQL fragment/constant, or a DAO query that takes the same arguments). Capture the standing cutoff once when the button is pressed so a row cannot change category between the list and the delete.
20	3. Clear only the affected ids in the delivery coordinator: do not call `invalidateAll()` for a scoped clear (that would cancel pending deliveries of rows the owner did not clear). Add a scoped coordinator operation and test that a pending High delivery survives a "clear Low". Retained notification actions are removed only for the cleared ids (`ServiceUtil.clearNotificationActions()` is all-or-nothing today; add a per-ids variant).
21	4. Button label names the scope: "Clear all" for All, "Clear high" etc. for a priority, and for the Cleared view something accurate (decide, log it as a default). Strings are copy (`writing-copy`).
22	5. No confirmation dialog (unchanged). Counts shown elsewhere (dashboard) update through the existing flows.
23	
24	## Not in scope (report, do not change)
25	
26	The dashboard's `FloodStatusWidget` "Clear All" (`OnDeleteAll`) and `StandingAlarmsWidget` "Clear All" (`OnClearAllStanding`); say in the report whether they have the same flaw.
27	
28	## Tests
29	
30	Test the design: (a) a parity test that the delete predicate and the list predicate select the same rows for a seeded set that includes standing-escalated rows (find how the existing data tests run Room/DAO; if none exist on the JVM, use the pure filter as the oracle and assert both queries are built from the shared fragment); (b) coordinator: scoped clear leaves other pending deliveries valid; (c) use case: scope -> repository call -> action removal for those ids only; (d) the screen's event carries the selected scope. Targeted runs only (`:notification_filter:*:test`).
31	# Per-category Clear
32	
33	Base `717faf6`, branch `fix/clear-per-category`. The notification inbox clears the selected priority across every page. **Clear all** still clears the entire inbox. **Delete cleared history** clears the entries listed in Cleared, which continues to use the prior priority filter when one is set.
34	
35	The click captures the cutoff used by the displayed query. Listing, selecting IDs, and deleting share one SQL predicate. Room selects IDs and deletes matching rows in the same transaction under the coordinator gate, using the predicate for both statements to avoid SQLite's ID parameter limit. The coordinator invalidates callbacks and removes retained actions by affected ID. It preserves callback capture order for eviction and allows newer callbacks to run after the transaction. Canceling those IDs' Android proxies is cleanup, so the callback mapper ignores Farhan's own cancellation while keeping user swipes actionable. A tab change hides the previous list until the new query loads.
36

# Per-category Clear: brief

Read first: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/agent-rules-2026-11-20.md`.
Worktree: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/clear-category`, branch `fix/clear-per-category`, base `717faf6`.
Report file: `research/clear-category-report.md`. Boat run name: `clear-category`.
You are the implementer (Sol): red tests first, then green, in this one run. Stop at green with tests passing; the orchestrator reviews next.

## The bug (owner, 2026-11-20)

"The clear button, in a particular category, only clears what is in that category, not everything overall."

In the notification inbox (`notification_filter_presentation/.../NotificationFilterScreen.kt`) the filter chips are Critical, High, Medium, Low, All, and Cleared. The bottom
button "Clear all" (line ~429) sends `OnDeleteAllNotifications` -> `DeleteAllNotifications` use case -> `core.coordinator.clearAll { repository.deleteAllNotificationsFromDB(); service.clearNotificationActions() }`
-> DAO `DELETE FROM notificationitementity`. So it removes every row, invalidates every pending delivery (`invalidateAll()`), and drops every retained action, whichever chip is selected.

## Required behaviour

1. With a priority chip selected the button clears exactly the rows that chip lists, on every page (the list shows 100 per page; the clear must not stop at the page). "All" keeps clearing everything. In the Cleared view the button acts only on the rows that view lists (no live inbox rows are touched).
2. The membership rule is the list's rule, which includes standing escalation: `NotificationInboxFilter.effectivePriority` (unread, not CRITICAL, older than the standing threshold hours counts one level lower) and the SQL `NotificationQueries.INBOX` with `standingCutoff`. Use ONE shared definition so list and clear cannot drift (a shared SQL fragment/constant, or a DAO query that takes the same arguments). Capture the standing cutoff once when the button is pressed so a row cannot change category between the list and the delete.
3. Clear only the affected ids in the delivery coordinator: do not call `invalidateAll()` for a scoped clear (that would cancel pending deliveries of rows the owner did not clear). Add a scoped coordinator operation and test that a pending High delivery survives a "clear Low". Retained notification actions are removed only for the cleared ids (`ServiceUtil.clearNotificationActions()` is all-or-nothing today; add a per-ids variant).
4. Button label names the scope: "Clear all" for All, "Clear high" etc. for a priority, and for the Cleared view something accurate (decide, log it as a default). Strings are copy (`writing-copy`).
5. No confirmation dialog (unchanged). Counts shown elsewhere (dashboard) update through the existing flows.

## Not in scope (report, do not change)

The dashboard's `FloodStatusWidget` "Clear All" (`OnDeleteAll`) and `StandingAlarmsWidget` "Clear All" (`OnClearAllStanding`); say in the report whether they have the same flaw.

## Tests

Test the design: (a) a parity test that the delete predicate and the list predicate select the same rows for a seeded set that includes standing-escalated rows (find how the existing data tests run Room/DAO; if none exist on the JVM, use the pure filter as the oracle and assert both queries are built from the shared fragment); (b) coordinator: scoped clear leaves other pending deliveries valid; (c) use case: scope -> repository call -> action removal for those ids only; (d) the screen's event carries the selected scope. Targeted runs only (`:notification_filter:*:test`).
# Per-category Clear

Base `717faf6`, branch `fix/clear-per-category`. The notification inbox clears the selected priority across every page. **Clear all** still clears the entire inbox. **Delete cleared history** clears the entries listed in Cleared, which continues to use the prior priority filter when one is set.

The click captures the cutoff used by the displayed query. Listing, selecting IDs, and deleting share one SQL predicate. Room selects IDs and deletes matching rows in the same transaction under the coordinator gate, using the predicate for both statements to avoid SQLite's ID parameter limit. The coordinator invalidates callbacks and removes retained actions by affected ID. It preserves callback capture order for eviction and allows newer callbacks to run after the transaction. Canceling those IDs' Android proxies is cleanup, so the callback mapper ignores Farhan's own cancellation while keeping user swipes actionable. A tab change hides the previous list until the new query loads.

## Regression tests

- The first Boat run used the new entry-point signatures with the old global behavior. Five assertions failed as expected for SQL membership, pending High delivery, scoped repository and action calls, click scope, and label mapping. Log `/tmp/boat-run/clear-category-20261120T115435Z-c18a9d.log`.
- The focused proxy callback run failed as expected when Farhan's own proxy cancellation was classified as a source app removal. Log `/tmp/boat-run/clear-category-20261120T115806Z-1c32f0.log`.
- The final Boat run passed all 179 targeted JVM tests with zero skips. Domain 155, data 21, presentation 3. Tasks were `:notification_filter:notification_filter_{domain,data,presentation}:testDebugUnitTest`. Log `/tmp/boat-run/clear-category-20261120T120013Z-5e8772.log`. `git diff --check` passed.
- Changes to existing test files were limited to extending the SQLite JDBC fixture's parameter binding for deletes, adding regression cases to the SQL, coordinator, and removal mapper suites, and implementing the new repository method in the dashboard-summary fake as an unsupported write. Existing assertions and red expectations are intact.

## Scope and limits

The flood widget dispatches a global delete, which also removes rows outside the flood window. The standing widget pages through its standing predicate and deletes the matching rows individually. The dashboard handlers were outside this change.

The JVM run exercises the actual SQL via SQLite JDBC and the screen's click dispatch and label mapping via presentation state. The app-generated Room DAO, rendering on a device, and real Android notification callbacks remain unverified. No issue reached the 30-minute flag threshold.

+    // why: CLAIM(inbox-clear-routing) keeps distinct storage and action operations for All, a priority, and Cleared.
+    // catches: global delete for a scoped request, dropping the cutoff or cleared flag, and clearing unrelated actions.
+    @Test fun `clear forwards the scope and drops only actions for deleted ids`() = runTest {
+        val calls = mutableListOf<List<Any?>>()
+        val repository = recordingPort<NotificationRepository> { name, args ->
+            calls.add(listOf(name) + args)
+            when (name) {
+                "deleteInboxNotifications" -> if (args.first() == true) listOf("history") else listOf("low-1", "low-2")
+                "deleteAllNotificationsFromDB" -> Unit
+                else -> error("Unexpected repository call $name")
+            }
+        }
+        val service = recordingPort<ServiceUtil> { name, args ->
+            check(name == "clearNotificationActions")
+            calls.add(listOf(name) + args)
+            Unit
+        }
+        val windows = threeWindows(8)
+        val h = DeliveryHarness(windows)
+        val book = FakeScheduleBookStore(ScheduleSnapshot(ScheduleBook(windows), DeliveryBudgetState()))
+        val core = NotificationCore(book, h.rows, h.budget, h.poster, h.environment, TEN_AM_DENVER) {}
+        val clear = DeleteAllNotifications(repository, core, service)
+
+        clear(InboxClearScope.Priority(LOW), standingCutoff = 500)
+        clear(InboxClearScope.Cleared(HIGH), standingCutoff = 700)
+        clear(InboxClearScope.All, standingCutoff = 900)
+
+        assertThat(calls).containsExactly(
+            listOf("deleteInboxNotifications", false, LOW, 500L),
+            listOf("clearNotificationActions", listOf("low-1", "low-2")),
+            listOf("deleteInboxNotifications", true, HIGH, 700L),
+            listOf("clearNotificationActions", listOf("history")),
+            listOf("deleteAllNotificationsFromDB"),
+            listOf("clearNotificationActions"),
+        ).inOrder()
+    }
+
+    private inline fun <reified T> recordingPort(crossinline record: (String, List<Any?>) -> Any?): T =
+        T::class.java.cast(Proxy.newProxyInstance(T::class.java.classLoader, arrayOf(T::class.java)) { _, method, args ->
+            val parameters = args.orEmpty().toList()
+            // Kotlin passes a continuation to suspend interface methods.
+            record(method.name, parameters.takeWhile { it !is kotlin.coroutines.Continuation<*> })
+        })!!
+}

+import ly.com.tahaben.notification_filter_domain.model.NotificationPriority.HIGH

+import org.junit.Test
+
+class NotificationFilterClearEventTest {
+    // why: CLAIM(inbox-clear-event) carries the visible filter and does not limit the operation to its page.
+    // catches: emitting All unconditionally, losing the priority on the Cleared tab, or reading the page as the scope.
+    @Test fun `clear click dispatches the selected tab scope`() {
+        val events = mutableListOf<NotificationFilterEvent>()

+        NotificationFilterState(showCleared = true, priorityFilter = HIGH, standingCutoff = 700).dispatchClear { events += it }
+        NotificationFilterState(showCleared = true).dispatchClear { events += it }
+

+            NotificationFilterEvent.OnClearNotifications(InboxClearScope.All, 0),
+            NotificationFilterEvent.OnClearNotifications(InboxClearScope.Priority(LOW), 500),
+            NotificationFilterEvent.OnClearNotifications(InboxClearScope.Cleared(HIGH), 700),
+            NotificationFilterEvent.OnClearNotifications(InboxClearScope.Cleared(null), 0),
+        ).inOrder()
+    }
+
+    // why: CLAIM(inbox-clear-event) names the scope before the user presses the button.
+    // catches: a generic Clear all label on any scoped view, or focusing on the prior priority in Cleared.
+    @Test fun `clear button label names the selected tab`() {
+        assertThat(NotificationFilterState().clearLabel).isEqualTo(R.string.clear_inbox_all)
+        assertThat(NotificationFilterState(priorityFilter = CRITICAL).clearLabel).isEqualTo(R.string.clear_inbox_critical)
+        assertThat(NotificationFilterState(priorityFilter = HIGH).clearLabel).isEqualTo(R.string.clear_inbox_high)
+        assertThat(NotificationFilterState(priorityFilter = MEDIUM).clearLabel).isEqualTo(R.string.clear_inbox_medium)
+        assertThat(NotificationFilterState(priorityFilter = LOW).clearLabel).isEqualTo(R.string.clear_inbox_low)
+        assertThat(NotificationFilterState(showCleared = true, priorityFilter = HIGH).clearLabel)
+            .isEqualTo(R.string.clear_inbox_history)
+    }
+}

# Usage permission fix: report

Status: verified and committed on `fix/usage-permission-package`. Not pushed.

## Review of the diff

Diff is correct: `checkUsagePermission()`, the two "ignore Farhan" filters in `UsageOverviewViewModel` and `WidgetWorker` now use the runtime package name.

Grep of the whole repo for `ly.com.tahaben.farhan` used as a package name:

- Legitimate (namespace, class names, component names): `app/build.gradle.kts` namespace and test runner, manifest `package`, `Class.forName("ly.com.tahaben.farhan.MainActivity")` (BroadcastReceiverNotification, UsageWidget), `context.packageName + "/ly.com.tahaben.farhan.service.AccessibilityService"` (class part, correct), `widget.WidgetConfigActivity`, `SettingsRecoveryIntegrationTest` component names, fixture strings in `MergeDaysUsageDurationTest`.
- **Same bug class, not fixed (outside this diff):** `screen_grayscale_data/.../GrayscaleUtilImpl.kt:31` runs `pm grant ly.com.tahaben.farhan android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` as root. On the installed `farhan_alpha` build this grants to a package that is not installed, so the root path never grants. Should be `context.packageName`.
- **Stale test (outside this diff):** `app/src/androidTest/.../ExampleInstrumentedTest.kt:20` asserts `appContext.packageName == "ly.com.tahaben.farhan"`; it fails on the alpha id (`SettingsRecoveryIntegrationTest` already asserts `farhan_alpha`).
- `app/release/output-metadata.json` has applicationId `ly.com.tahaben.farhan`: an old release artifact, not source.
- `UsageOverviewE2E` change compiles against the new constructor; it uses an inline fully qualified `InstrumentationRegistry`, which works but is untidy.

## Orchestrator decisions applied

1. `GrayscaleUtilImpl.getSecureSettingsPermissionWithRoot()` now runs `pm grant ${context.packageName} ...`. `context` is already a constructor field of the class, so it was in scope with no wiring change. The path is reachable: `GrayscaleScreen.kt:130` shows the button only when RootBeer reports a rooted device, and the button calls `GrayscaleViewModel.askForSecureSettingsPermissionWithRoot()`. Not run on a rooted device (the emulator is not rooted for `su`); only compiled.
2. Changed existing test: `ExampleInstrumentedTest.useAppContext` now asserts `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha` (was the namespace, which could never match). Not run on the emulator; compiled only.
3. `UsageOverviewE2E` now imports `InstrumentationRegistry` instead of the inline fully qualified call.
4. `app/release/output-metadata.json` untouched.

## Build and unit tests (Boat, run `usage-permission`)

Final run: `:usage_overview:usage_overview_domain:test :usage_overview:usage_overview_presentation:testDebugUnitTest :screen_grayscale:screen_grayscale_data:compileDebugKotlin :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin :app:assembleDebug` — PASS (exit 0, 62 s). Log `/tmp/boat-run/usage-permission-20261120T115914Z-d27931.log`. The first run (before decisions 1-3) also passed: same usage tasks, 166 s, log `/tmp/boat-run/usage-permission-20261120T115128Z-36673c.log`.
Unit tests that ran: 8 tests in 5 classes (usage_overview_domain: ExampleUnitTest, CalculateUsageDurationTest, IsDayOverTest, MergeDaysUsageDurationTest; usage_overview_presentation: ExampleUnitTest); 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. None of them touches the permission check, which is Android-bound.

## Emulator proof (AVD `farhan-notification-pilot`, API 35, sandbox `bx_bngcafgz`)

Evidence in `research/usage-permission/` (screenshots and uiautomator text).

| Step | APK | `appops get ... GET_USAGE_STATS` | Usage page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | baseline `farhan-notification-pilot/.../app-debug.apk` (10:02) | `allow` | "Usage permission is not granted :(" / "Farhan needs usage access to display your usage information" / Grant access / How? (`baseline-usage.png`, `baseline-usage.txt`) |
| After | fixed APK from this worktree | `allow; time=+7s344ms ago` | Usage page: date row (Today), Total usage "1" and "41" (hours and minutes), category percentages, app list (`fixed-usage.png`, `fixed-usage.txt`) |

The `time=+7s...ago` on the fixed run is AppOps recording the app's own `GET_USAGE_STATS` use; the baseline shows no such access.

Caveats:
- The fixed APK shown on the emulator was built before decisions 1-3; those touch the grayscale root command and test files only, and the final build was recompiled and passed, but the final APK was not re-installed.
- The baseline APK came from the shared pilot run directory, built 10:02 on the base commit's tree as the brief states; I did not rebuild it.
- The "ignore Farhan" filters are not proven on the device: the setting is off by default (`filterFarhan = false`), and the fixed run still lists Farhan-alpha, as expected with the setting off.
- Emulator left running on the sandbox for the orchestrator to reuse or stop.

## Pure seam?

No worthwhile one. The only logic changed is which string is passed to AppOps; extracting it to a JVM-testable function would test `context.packageName` being passed through, which restates the change. Not built.

# A visual language for Farhan notifications

-Start with two views of the same notification. Inbox should show what happened and retain the original message. Overview should show when Farhan may deliver it and what could hold it back. A six-message chat is one conversation to read and six pending entries to account for. Those views can share the underlying records without implying that their counts mean the same thing.

[Scheduled Summary](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/view-and-respond-to-notifications-iph6534c01bc/ios) · [Focus filters](https://support.apple.com/en-euro/guide/iphone/iphd6288a67f/26/ios/26) |

+| Microsoft Adaptive Cards | A JSON card describes content and the host renders it in its own style. A verified payment payload could fill an amount and merchant template that inherits Farhan’s theme. [Adaptive Cards](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/adaptive-cards/) |

+| Observable Plot and Vega-Lite | Marks encode fields through positions, lengths and other channels, and facets repeat the same plotting frame. Draw source activity as equal-scale rows, with the same hourly bins for every app. [Observable Plot marks](https://observablehq.github.io/plot/features/marks) · [Vega-Lite facets](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/docs/facet.html) |

+| Tufte sparklines and small multiples | A small series can sit beside its label and final value. Repeat the same scale for each app, and label a count such as “13 posts in 2 h” beside the strip so a burst remains legible without reading the whole series. [Sparkline theory and practice](https://www.edwardtufte.com/notebook/sparkline-theory-and-practice-edward-tufte/) · [Clinical data display example](https://www.edwardtufte.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Summarizing-Clinical-Psychiatric-Data-Seth-M-Powsner-Edward-R-Tufte.pdf) |

+| Gantt charts and git graphs | A Gantt chart aligns spans against a time axis, and a git graph keeps distinct histories in lanes. Use budget windows as spans and priorities as lanes. Use an explicit link to its source post when a send mark can be paired with it. [Mermaid Gantt](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/gantt) · [Mermaid gitGraph](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/gitgraph) |

+| Superhuman | Split Inbox puts messages that match a rule into their own view. Let a review pass bring “Waiting for budget” together with an explicit rule and an item count. [Custom Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005636204941-Custom-Split-Inbox) |

+| HEY Imbox | Imbox, Feed and Paper Trail give people separate places for correspondence, things to browse, and receipts. Give recurring news and transaction receipts compact group headers inside Farhan’s chosen Inbox, using explicit rules. [The Imbox](https://help.hey.com/article/759-imbox) · [HEY mail views](https://help.hey.com/article/903-how-can-i-see-all-my-emails) |

+| Gmail categories | Default Inbox categories can group mail automatically, and users can move a misfiled message. A Farhan kind view could expose its fallback and allow a deliberate override if kinds prove useful. [Gmail categories](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/3094499) |

+| Linear Triage | Incoming issues await a decision such as accept or decline. Borrow the visible pending state for cases where the user can genuinely decide what happens next. [Linear Triage](https://linear.app/docs/triage) |

+| Things and Todoist | Things can drop a captured task into Inbox for later organization. Todoist’s Inbox is the default home for a task with no project. A quiet Farhan row can stay readable before the user decides whether to open or clear it. [Things Quick Entry](https://culturedcode.com/things/support/articles/2249437/) · [Todoist Inbox](https://www.todoist.com/help/todoist/get-started/use-the-inbox-in-todoist-HwHvYErS) |

+| Bloomberg Terminal | A market monitor places aligned fields alongside changing values so comparisons happen in place. A compact Farhan panel can line up each source’s arrival count, pending count and points in the same columns. Keep the long text one tap away. [Bloomberg Terminal](https://professional.bloomberg.com/products/bloomberg-terminal/) |

+| Apple Watch glanceables | A complication fits a small fact into a watch-face slot. An Overview header can give one number and its unit, such as “10 pts left,” with the window printed beside it. [Apple complications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/complications) |

+| Teenage Engineering OP-1 | The hardware uses repeated symbols and shared color across related functions. Give a handful of Farhan kinds fixed silhouettes and repeat them where their meaning stays the same. [OP-1 mode controls](https://teenage.engineering/guides/op-1/original/main-modes) |

+| Material Symbols | Fill, weight and optical size are separate axes. Let fill denote a selected control and tune weight for legibility at small sizes. Keep priority encoded by its own shape and label. [Material Symbols guide](https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/material_symbols) |

+| Traffic lights | The vertical red, yellow, green order adds a positional cue. Keep the location and shape of Farhan priority markers consistent and put the priority name beside them. [FHWA MUTCD, Part 4](https://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/pdfs/11th_Editionr1/part4r1.pdf) |

+| TCAS | Traffic Collision Avoidance System displays distinguish an amber circle traffic advisory from a red square resolution advisory. The transferable idea is redundant shape and color for states requiring different responses. Farhan can use its own labelled priority shapes. [FAA TCAS II introduction](https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/TCAS%20II%20V7.1%20Intro%20booklet.pdf) |

Show one persistent “Budget blocked” or “Flood active” cue in Overview. Open the rows affected and state why. [FAA Flightcrew Alerting](https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_25.1322-1.pdf) |

Overview counts posts by kind using the same glyphs and opens a scoped Inbox. | Read a thread once, see the time of an event or identify what a bank alert is asking. | Card heights vary. Group headers hide earlier snippets until opened. | One thumb can open a whole card. A few templates share priority marks and a plain fallback. |

Overview aligns priority lanes and budget windows. | Answer “When will this show up?” and see the one chat that misses 11:00. | Separates related posts when only some fit a batch. Clock and date labels need room. | Makes cadence and budget visible inside the chosen navigation. A vertical list works on a narrow phone. |

+| Source activity strips | Inbox shows equal-height app groups with count and latest subject. Overview adds small multiples of arrivals, with shared time bins and numeric counts. | Trace who produced a burst and spot which app stayed quiet. | Compresses the content and can blur separate conversations. One app may dominate a shared scale. | Useful at flood scale and legible without color. Whole rows open the posts. |

+| Quiet list | Inbox shows source, subject and time on one or two lines with a small labelled priority cue. Overview shows the next eligible batch and the number waiting, with details on tap. | Scroll quickly and find a specific subject with little visual noise. | The body, exact budget, reason for waiting, and related items need another tap. | Lowest Compose cost and a comfortable dense mode. Keep visible text at large font sizes by letting rows grow. |

Overview shows a labelled condition and its count only while it applies. | Find something the user can act on, such as a verified bank review request or a queue blocked by a full window. | A false action signal harms trust. A routine event may move further down the screen. | Suits standing alarms and flood status with an evidence-based trigger. Priority and “requires action” remain separate facts. |

+| Message thread | Stack by source and stable thread identity. Lead with the latest sender and snippet. Expand to original posts. Without an identity, show independent rows or a labelled app bucket. |
+| Payment | Put amount, currency and merchant as reported on one line, with the source and event time below. Prefer the generic row when fields are ambiguous or absent. |
+| Calendar | Put the source-reported local event time next to the title. Keep its location and the source post time labelled separately. |
+| Delivery update | Put the current shipment stage first. Show a stage strip and the source ETA if those fields are available. |
+| Alert | Start with the reported condition and what the sender asks. Surface an action only where Farhan has a supported action reference. |
+| One-time code | Show a labelled masked code. Keep any reveal in the individual item and keep codes out of aggregates and previews. Use a known kind or trustworthy source metadata. |
+| Generic | Show original app, title, text, post time and priority. An unknown kind retains the same access to delivery details. |

+For a pilot, the existing category and captured data can support a generic card and category marks. Android’s notification API can expose a shortcut ID, style extras and progress where apps publish them. It offers no common typed schema for arbitrary bank, parcel and calendar messages. Add narrow capture rules at intake and select a specialized card only when evidence is sufficient. Keep classification read-only with respect to delivery. The mock-up assumes usable thread, calendar, parcel and code fields for the demo. It groups six distinct records. A single MessagingStyle notification containing six message lines would still be one queued record with one point charge. [Android Notification API](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Notification) · [Android conversations](https://developer.android.com/social-and-messaging/guides/communication/notifications-conversations) · [Current intake][service]

+Low to medium cost for a generic card and one verified thread variant, roughly 2–4 developer days for a pilot once the source metadata is settled. Keep `LazyColumn`, existing row actions, filters and `NotificationListItem` as the fallback. Borrow expand, page and open behavior from `RecentBatchesWidget`. Reuse `CategoryBreakdownWidget` for category totals and the weighted segments in `PriorityDistributionWidget` for a compact count display. The mock-up’s counts by presentation kind would need their own aggregation. Cost increases if thread grouping has to span pages, or if kind-specific data needs a storage migration. Keep one canonical item ID and individual dismiss/read behavior within a group. Start with the verified conversation and defer transaction, parcel, calendar and code renderers until useful metadata is demonstrated. [Inbox screen][inbox] · [Existing row][row] · [Recent Batches][recentWidget] · [Category Breakdown][categoryWidget] · [Priority Distribution][distWidget]

+Medium cost for a next-opportunity card by priority, roughly 2–3 developer days if it shows only cadence ticks and the active balance. Reuse the cadence settings from `PriorityDeliveryWidget`, windows from `NotificationScheduleWidget`, and the balance and progress indicator from `BudgetSpendWidget`. Use Compose text for times, amounts and tap routes, with a small Canvas or ordinary Compose layout for lines and marks. Keep the dashboard's existing top-chatter and standing sections available. A forecast that assigns individual rows to batches is higher cost, roughly a week for a bounded pilot. It needs a coherent read-only snapshot, explicit eligibility and hold reasons, and parity with coordinator ordering, live-source gating and limits. Project a bounded horizon and show “Waiting for budget” or “No estimate” beyond it. Refresh on queue, budget, schedule, time zone or clock changes. Ignore stale forecasts and use the dated schedule that applies to each future day. Recent Batches can supply its disclosure pattern. Its source-grouped post timestamps cannot identify the delivery history. The current spend log timestamps charged sends and lacks an item ID. A precise per-item history would need its own record. [Dashboard state][dashboardState] · [Delivery settings widget][priorityWidget] · [Schedule widget][scheduleWidget] · [Budget widget][budgetWidget] · [Delivery policy][policy] · [Delivery coordinator][coordinator] · [Spend entry][spend] · [Recent Batches aggregation][batches]

+The Inbox mock includes the delivery view to test whether it is worth opening from Overview. I would start with the two surfaces above and keep the choice of a second full Inbox mode open. The sample is a 10:42 snapshot with default cadences, newest-first chat ordering, and a custom budget. Five High items can use the remaining 10 points at 11:00. The sixth waits for 12:00, when it and two Medium items use 10 of the new 12 points. The Low item can use 8 of 10 points at midnight. The spend at 10:42 comes from earlier items already cleared from the Inbox. The illustrative forecast assumes no further arrivals, cancellations, delivery failures or other gate changes.
+1. When you reach for Inbox after a busy hour, do you want to catch up by conversation or see what Farhan is still holding?
+2. Should the timeline say “Next eligible at 11:00” first, or is it worth estimating which five messages can fit then?
+3. Can verified chat threads collapse by default? For apps with weak metadata, do you prefer independent rows or an explicit app bucket?
+4. Which would earn a second renderer after chat? A bank alert, an appointment, a shipment, or a one-time code?
+5. How much should an Inbox card reveal for bank and code notifications before you open it?

content.text:
Both reviews are done. I edited nothing in either worktree. To check what the authors hadn't, I compiled `:app:compileDebugKotlin` for branch A on Boat (run `review-clear`, from a shared clone). It passes. Room's generated `NotificationDao_FarhanDatabase_Impl.clearInbox` wraps the select and the delete in one `withTransaction`. The author had only compiled the `notification_filter` modules, and Room generates this DAO in `:app`.

## A. fix/clear-per-category (10dd0d1)

What works:
- **Shared rule:** listing, ID selection and deletion are all built from one SQL predicate (`INBOX_PREDICATE`), at the cutoff of the query on screen.
- **Atomic and limit-safe:** the select and delete run in one Room transaction, inside the coordinator's gate with `NonCancellable`. Nothing binds an ID list, so SQLite's variable limit can't be hit.
- **Same set:** the IDs deleted are exactly the IDs whose delivery events are invalidated.
- **Stale callbacks:** a stale callback for a cleared ID is rejected. A callback captured after `clearOrder` still gets through.
- **All:** unchanged.

**Findings, most severe first:**

1. **[should]** `notification_filter_presentation/.../NotificationFilterState.kt:25`, `showCleared -> Cleared(priorityFilter)`
   - **Claim:** the "Delete cleared history" label promises more than the button deletes.
   - **Scenario:** in the chip row (`NotificationFilterScreen.kt:238`), tapping Cleared deselects every priority chip, but the hidden `priorityFilter` stays set. Tap Low, then Cleared: the list shows only cleared Low rows (an old bug). Pressing "Delete cleared history" then deletes only cleared Low rows, and cleared High history stays.
   - **Fix:** when switching into Cleared, `OnToggleClearedView` also sets `priorityFilter = null`, so what's selected and what's deleted match. Then `InboxClearScope.Cleared` needs no priority.

2. **[should]** `NotificationFilterViewModel.kt:122` and `:85`
   - **Claim:** nothing tests the ViewModel's routing, so the owner's bug can come back with all 179 tests green.
   - **Scenario 1:** change the handler to `notificationFilterUseCases.deleteAllNotifications()` (the old global clear). Every test passes.
   - **Scenario 2:** drop `standingCutoff = query.standingCutoff`. The click then sends cutoff 0, so clearing Low misses aged Medium rows that the list shows under Low. Every test still passes.
   - `NotificationFilterClearEventTest` only exercises `state.dispatchClear` with a hand-built state.
   - **Fix:** one ViewModel test with a fake repository: select Low, let a page arrive, dispatch the clear, then assert the use case received `Priority(LOW)` and the query's own cutoff.

3. **[should]** `notification_filter_presentation/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`
   - **Claim:** the All label lost its translations.
   - **Scenario:** the old label was core's `R.string.clear_all`, translated into ca, fr, ar, es, pl and ta. A French user who saw "Tout effacer" now sees English "Clear all". The new strings exist only in English.
   - **Fix:** keep core's `clear_all` for the All scope, or carry its translations over.

4. **[should]** `NotificationFilterViewModel.kt:142` and `:150`
   - **Claim:** tapping any chip now briefly shows "No notifications".
   - **Scenario:** the lists are emptied until the new query emits, so the screen's empty state (`Screen:259`) renders, and the Clear button disappears. Hiding a stale list is the right call, but the screen tells the user the inbox is empty. Not checked on a device.
   - **Fix:** make the list nullable or add `isLoading`. While loading, render nothing and hide the button.

5. **[should]** `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:210` and `DeleteAllNotifications.kt:25`, Cleared scope only
   - **Claim:** deleting cleared history still invalidates events and cancels proxies one ID at a time, inside the gate.
   - **Scenario A:** history can be thousands of rows. That means thousands of `NotificationManager.cancel` binder calls for proxies that don't exist (cleared rows have none), while deliveries wait on the gate.
   - **Scenario B:** a source app re-posts a key whose old row is in history, and that callback was captured just before the press. It is rejected as `Cleared` and never reaches the inbox. The brief says the Cleared view touches no live rows.
   - **Fix:** for `Cleared`, delete under the gate and remove retained actions, but skip `invalidateDeleted` and the proxy cancels.

6. **[nit]** `DeleteAllNotifications.kt` / `NotificationQueries.INBOX_CLEAR`
   - **Claim:** a row can be deleted before the user ever sees it.
   - **Scenario:** a matching row arrives after the press but before the gate is free. The gate can be held by a batch tick posting up to 256 proxies. The clear deletes that row unseen. The old All clear behaved the same way.
   - **Fix:** capture a high-water mark when the button is pressed (largest rowid or `clickedAt`) and add it to the predicate.

7. **[nit]** `NotificationFilterViewModel.kt:122`
   - **Claim:** the page number isn't reset after a clear.
   - **Scenario:** clear Low from page 3 and you land on an empty page 3 with "Newer" still enabled.
   - **Fix:** set `page = 0` on clear.

8. **[nit]** `NotificationDeliveryCoordinatorTest`
   - **Claim:** nothing pins the `event.order <= clearOrder` guard at `:226`.
   - **Scenario:** remove the guard so every deleted ID is marked removed. All tests still pass, yet a post captured during `delete()` would be dropped.
   - **Fix:** capture an event inside the `delete` lambda and assert that its arrival is accepted.

9. **[nit]** Naming and signatures:
   - `DeleteAllNotifications` now routes scoped clears; rename it `ClearInbox`.
   - `NotificationRepositoryImpl.kt:61` hardcodes `search = ""` while `InboxQuery` has a `search` field. Pass the same query shape (without paging) so a future search box can't drift from the clear.
   - `NotificationRemovalMapper.kt:7`: make `ownProxy` required instead of defaulting to `false`.
   - I checked the mapper change against the other paths that cancel Farhan's own proxy (single delete, mark as cleared, failed open). Each records its own removal through `clearInbox`, so ignoring the proxy's own cancel callback loses nothing.

**VERDICT A: CHANGES.** No must items. Items 1–3 should land before the owner sees it.
- Correctness 7/10
- Concurrency 8/10
- Tests 6/10
- Legibility 7/10

## B. fix/usage-permission-package (653b60b)

The fix is complete. I searched the whole repo for the package name as a string:
- The only usage-access check is `UsageRepositoryImpl`. Report generation goes through the same check, so reports are fixed too.
- Every other `ly.com.tahaben.farhan…` literal is a class or component name, which is correct: `Class.forName(...MainActivity)`, the accessibility component, and the widget `configure` attribute.
- Hilt can supply the new `@ApplicationContext` parameter. The E2E test is its only direct constructor call. `WidgetWorker` uses its own `context`, so nothing else needs to change.

1. **[should]** `research/usage-permission/fixed-usage.png`
   - **Claim:** the "after" screenshot doesn't show what the report says.
   - **Scenario:** it shows the loading state ("--", NaN %, a spinner). The report says it shows total usage. The loaded data appears only in `fixed-usage.txt` (1 h 41 m, 53.5 % Productivity). The text dump does prove the fix, but this PNG would mislead in the PR body.
   - **Fix:** retake it after the screen loads. Separately, the loading state shows NaN % because of a division by zero. That bug is older than this branch; worth a ticket.

2. **[nit]** `scripts/profile-notifications.py:19`
   - **Claim:** same bug class as the fix.
   - **Scenario:** the default `--package` is `ly.com.tahaben.farhan`, so the script fails with "not installed" against the alpha build.
   - **Fix:** default to `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha`.

3. **[nit]** `UsageOverviewViewModel.kt`
   - **Claim:** injecting `Context` into a ViewModel only to read the package name couples it to Android.
   - **Fix:** expose the app's own package name from the repository or a use case. `ServiceUtil.getOwnPackageName()` already does this in notification_filter.

4. **[nit]** `ExampleInstrumentedTest.kt:20`: assert against `BuildConfig.APPLICATION_ID` instead of a second hardcoded ID.

**VERDICT B: OK.** Retake the screenshot before it goes into a PR.
- Correctness 9/10
- Concurrency 10/10 (no concurrent code touched)
- Tests 5/10 (no automated check of the fix; the emulator evidence is good)
- Legibility 8/10

Ready for the pushback or question.

Nothing cancels Farhan's proxy for that id, so a cleared row can still have a posted proxy. My earlier claim that cleared rows have no proxies was wrong, so I'm conceding that and skipping the proxy step.

I'm checking whether invalidating a cleared row adds anything beyond the cancel: it seems to only drop a new post captured before the clear, which would otherwise bring the row back. Whether that post counts as stale is the open question.

Binder calls are the cost here: `NotificationManager.cancel` makes an IPC per id even when the id doesn't exist. Since the per-id loop already runs under one gate hold without suspending, the real fix is one read of `manager.activeNotifications`, cancelling only the intersection with the ids (proxies are capped at 1024), and removing actions for all ids in memory. content.text:
Three answers from the code. I edited nothing.

**1. You're right about proxies; I withdraw finding 5 as written.**
- **A source cancel leaves the proxy posted.** In `NotificationService.kt:328-341`, a source-app removal does `captureEvent(originalId, removed = true)`, then `actionStore.remove`, then `Work.Removed`. At `:84` that becomes `coordinator.onRemoved`, which calls `rows.markCleared(id)` (`NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:200`). Nothing on that path calls `cancelProxy`. So a row that Farhan already delivered and the source app then cancels sits in Cleared with its proxy still posted. Mark-as-cleared (`clearInbox`, `:207`) does cancel the proxy through `deleteNotificationIntent`. Arrival-side `markCleared` (`:174`, `:253`, `:272`, `:283`) happens before or instead of a post. But the source-cancel path alone disproves "cleared rows have no proxies". The Cleared clear has to keep cancelling proxies.
- **Invalidation for Cleared rows is mostly redundant, but harmless to keep.** Every path above records an event with `removed = true`, so `stale()` already rejects any callback captured before the removal. The only extra thing `invalidateDeleted` does for a cleared ID is drop a fresh re-post captured after the removal but before the press. Without the clear, that post would revive the row. That's a narrow edge, so I'm downgrading it to a nit. Keeping one code path for every scope is simpler. Don't special-case Cleared.
- **The cost is the binder calls, not the loop.** `NotificationManager.cancel(tag, id)` is an IPC every time, because the client can't know whether the ID is posted. The loop already runs in one gate hold with no per-ID suspension: `clearActions(ids)` is a plain function called once inside `NonCancellable`. So batching is already in place and changes nothing. The cheap fix that works for every scope:
  - read `manager.activeNotifications` once, the same pattern `cancelAllProxies` uses;
  - intersect it with `ids` and cancel only those (live proxies are capped at `MAX_LIVE_PROXIES = 1024`);
  - remove the retained actions for every ID in memory.

  That gives one IPC plus at most the live proxies. Severity: should, keyed to how large history can grow, which I didn't measure.

**2. Agreed: decline finding 6.** All behaves the same way, and a row that arrives while the gate is busy can't be told apart from one that arrives a moment after the press. A one-line note in the report is enough.

**3. The flash is new in this branch.** At base 717faf6, `NotificationFilterViewModel.kt:149-158`:
```kotlin
is NotificationFilterEvent.OnSetPriorityFilter -> {
    state = state.copy(priorityFilter = event.priority)
    state = state.copy(page = 0)
    getNotifications()
}
...
NotificationFilterEvent.OnToggleClearedView -> {
    state = state.copy(showCleared = !state.showCleared, page = 0)
    getNotifications()
}
```
Base kept the old list until the new query emitted. This branch adds `filteredNotifications = emptyList(), clearedNotifications = emptyList()` at `:142` and `:150`. The empty list is what triggers "No notifications" (`Screen:259`), so it's in scope.

The branch has a reason for hiding the list: it stops the user from pressing "Clear high" while the Low list is still on screen. The fix is a loading state, not reverting the blanking: render nothing and hide the button until the first emission.

**Revised verdicts:**
- **A: CHANGES** (findings 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, plus finding 5 reworked as the one-IPC proxy cancel). Correctness 7, concurrency 8, tests 6, legibility 7.
- **B: OK** with the should-fixes you accepted. Correctness 9, concurrency 10, tests 5, legibility 8.
